en.title: Anthropic Files IPO Application for November Debut
en.dek: Anthropic has filed for an IPO, aiming to list on Nasdaq in November and raise capital for AI development.
facts: Anthropic filed IPO documents with the SEC.
Shares will trade on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the offering.
The prospectus does not disclose share count or price, but the company could be valued up to $2 trillion.
Revenue rose from $1.2 billion to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, while net loss grew from $13 billion to $80.7 billion.
body: Anthropic filed its IPO documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, targeting a November debut on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The offering is led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, with both new shares and existing investor holdings to be sold.

The 333‑page prospectus does not specify the number of shares or the offering price, but it indicates a potential valuation of up to $2 trillion. The first trading price reported was $150, following an issue price of $135.

Financial data in the prospectus shows revenue increasing from $1.2 billion in the same period of 2025 to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, while the net loss expanded from $13 billion to $80.7 billion due to high costs for data‑center construction and other infrastructure. The high costs reflect the company's investment in building data centers for AI.

The company stated that the IPO will provide liquidity to fund the development of advanced AI models, which requires significant investment in chips, data centers, and related infrastructure. It also highlighted risks such as misuse, loss of human control, authoritarian misuse, and economic disruption.
en.context: Anthropic is a U.S. AI company known for its Claude chatbot. The IPO seeks to secure capital for expanding its AI capabilities amid intense competition.
